user.title: Welcome to Tesla LoadPilot
user.description: LoadPilot adjusts your vehicle's charging so your home never exceeds your electricity contract. Everything runs locally - no cloud. First, tell us which meter your installation uses.

data_description.country_profile: Profiles marked “preview” ship as firmware skeletons and have not been validated in production yet.

nodes.title: Your two LoadPilot nodes
nodes.description: LoadPilot relies on two small ESP32 nodes already set up with ESPHome: one next to the wall connector (it talks to it), one next to the meter (it measures). If you followed the guide without renaming, keep the suggested values.

data_description.charger_node: ESPHome device name of the node wired to the wall connector (default: loadpilot-twc).
data_description.meter_node: ESPHome device name of the node reading your meter (default: loadpilot-meter).

electrical.title: Your electricity contract
electrical.description: These two settings are what keeps your main breaker happy. They are written into the charger node itself and keep working even when Home Assistant is off.

data_description.contract_preset: Pick your subscribed power to fill in the limit for you - or choose “Other” and enter the amps yourself below.
data_description.contract_limit_a: In France: 3 kVA single-phase = 15 A · 6 kVA = 30 A · 9 kVA = 45 A · 12 kVA = 60 A · 15 kVA = 75 A · 18 kVA = 90 A. Three-phase, per phase: 6 kVA = 10 A · 9 kVA = 15 A · 12 kVA = 20 A · 15 kVA = 25 A · 18 kVA = 30 A.
data_description.buffer_pct: With a 10% buffer, the car only uses 90% of your contract: the rest absorbs surges (an oven or a pump starting) without tripping the breaker.

mirror.title: Backup if the direct link goes down
mirror.description: Normally the meter node talks directly to the charger node. If that link goes down, Home Assistant can relay the measurements as a backup. Optional but recommended. Without it, if both the direct link and Home Assistant are unavailable, charging is blocked for safety (your contract is never exceeded).

data_description.current_l1: Pick the entities coming from your meter node.

confirm.title: Check before enabling
confirm.description: Meter: {country_profile}. Installation: {phases}-phase. Contract: {contract_limit_a} A per phase, {buffer_pct}% buffer - that leaves a budget of {budget_a} A per phase for the whole house, car included. These settings are written into the charger node: they stay active even when Home Assistant is off. Regulation itself is enabled from the LoadPilot card, not here.

error.charger_not_found: Charger node not found. It must be adopted in ESPHome and visible in Home Assistant before this step (see the firmware guide).
error.meter_not_found: Meter node not found. It must be adopted in ESPHome and visible in Home Assistant before this step (see the firmware guide).
error.budget_too_small: With these settings only {budget_a} A per phase remain for the whole house - the car will never be able to charge. Check the limit (in amps PER PHASE) and the buffer.
error.tri_limit_suspicious: {contract_limit_a} A per phase on three-phase is unusually high - did you enter the three-phase total, or a single-phase figure? Submit again without changing it to confirm.

abort.already_configured: This LoadPilot charger node is already configured.

init.title: LoadPilot options
init.description: Changes are written straight into the charger node. To change the country profile or the nodes, remove and re-add the integration.

data_description.contract_preset: Pick your subscribed power to fill in the limit for you - or choose “Other” and enter the amps yourself below.
data_description.buffer_pct: With a 10% buffer, the car only uses 90% of your contract: the rest absorbs surges without tripping the breaker.
data_description.configure_entity_mapping: Only for charger nodes whose entity names do not follow the standard LoadPilot firmware (historic installations). Leave off otherwise.

advanced_mapping.title: Advanced entity mapping
advanced_mapping.description: Map each LoadPilot signal to the actual entity of your charger node. Leave a field empty to use the standard name. Fields already empty for a signal your node does not provide stay declared absent - pick an entity to start tracking it again. Only the six current measures (published + measured, per phase) are required for regulation monitoring.

error.tri_limit_suspicious: {contract_limit_a} A per phase on three-phase is unusually high - did you enter the three-phase total, or a single-phase figure? Submit again without changing it to confirm.

set_bias.name: Set charging slowdown (bias)
set_bias.description: Deliberately slows the vehicle down by reserving amps for the rest of the house. 0 = no slowdown; the maximum (16 A on three-phase, 32 A on single-phase) = charging paused. The value ramps smoothly - the ramp is handled by the charger node.

amps.name: Reserved amps
amps.description: Amps taken away from the vehicle, per phase (0 to 16 on three-phase, 0 to 32 on single-phase, step 0.5).

pause.name: Pause charging
pause.description: Cleanly pauses vehicle charging by reserving the full bias (16 A on three-phase, 32 A on single-phase). The vehicle stops in a few minutes without error - the bias ramps smoothly, so a full single-phase pause takes longer. Resume with “Resume charging”.

resume.name: Resume charging
resume.description: Releases the pause (bias back to 0). The vehicle resumes charging on its own within a few minutes.

confirm.title: Firmware / integration version skew
confirm.description: The charger node runs package version {fw_version} while the integration is {integration_version}. Update the pinned ESPHome package `ref:` (or the HACS integration) so both match, then confirm. Regulation is NOT blocked by this skew.

confirm.title: No healthy measure source
confirm.description: The charger node is in fail-safe: both the UDP feed and the HA mirror are down, so it publishes full consumption and blocks charging (safe behaviour). Restore the meter node or the mirror entities, then confirm.

charger_node_missing.title: Charger node not found in Home Assistant

confirm.title: Charger node not found in Home Assistant
confirm.description: No entity of the charger node “{charger_node}” exists in Home Assistant (node offline since before startup, renamed, or removed from ESPHome). The node itself keeps regulating on its own - the control law lives in its firmware - but Home Assistant can no longer observe or adjust it. Restore the node under this exact name (or remove and re-add the integration with the right name), then confirm.
